column3: stressor
Clojure core adds value-class support to deftype in a release.
A competing library gives value classes through gen-class and an annotation, and takes most users.
closed-record removes its value-type dependency and emits value classes itself.
Users ask for the same defvaluetype source to work on ClojureScript and ClojureCLR.
Oracle stops Project Valhalla. No more EA builds are released.
A user defines a type with 2000 fields.
A popular library calls locking on value objects in a common code path.
A large user AOT-compiles an application on Java 8 and deploys it on a Valhalla JVM with policy error.
A code generator evaluates 100000 defvaluetype forms at run time.
Data scientists start to allocate arrays of one billion value objects.
Java-only teams load AOT value types with Class.forName and no Clojure source.
The only maintainer stops work for one year.
The maintainer's employer forbids publication of code that depends on EA JVMs.
The AI model provider replaces the model. The new model ignores Simplified Technical English and Ramora rules.
A second maintainer joins. They know the class-file format but not the Clojure compiler.
The closed-record author demands per-type fallback overrides and forks value-type.
The maintainer decides to merge value-type into closed-record.
Oracle changes the EA build licence: no use in CI without an agreement.
A court decides that shipping software that needs --add-exports of internal JDK packages breaks the JDK licence.
Clojars removes all EPL-licensed artifacts after a licence dispute.
A regulation requires signed, reproducible builds of all dependencies.
GitHub Actions stops free minutes for public repositories.
Each new JVM row doubles the matrix cells. CI cost increases 10 times.
A sponsor pays for support of five EA builds at the same time.
The price of the AI agent service triples.
Clojure 1.13 adds a hidden field to deftype classes and changes the constructor order.
Clojure removes the bundled clojure.asm package.
Clojure changes Compiler/LOADER so that let pushes a new loader.
Clojars closes.
The Scry test runner is abandoned and fails on a new Clojure release.
The next EA build renames the methods of jdk.internal.value.ValueClass.
A new EA build changes the ACC_STRICT_INIT value and the class version rule.
JEP 401 becomes final in JDK 28. The preview minor version and --enable-preview are not used.
The JVM replaces the NullRestricted annotation with a null-marker in field descriptors.
GraalVM native-image becomes the usual deployment target for Clojure applications.
CIDER starts to macroexpand each top-level form on each keystroke.
The java.lang.classfile API changes the signatures of ClassFile.of and its options.
A JIT defect in an EA build gives wrong values from flattened arrays.
A field tag names a class that a sibling plugin class loader defines.
AOT class files from a different JDK feature release are on the class path.
A production launcher sets value-type.fallback=wran.
A user persists serialized value objects and reads them on a fallback JVM.
Monitoring parses the capability report. A release adds and renames keys.
An attacker publishes a malicious fork on Clojars with a similar coordinate.
A deployment platform forbids custom class loaders.
A CVE in clojure.asm forces an urgent Clojure update.
A library writes nil into a non-nil field through Unsafe. An attacker uses the resulting NullPointerException.
An attacker takes the maintainer's GitHub account and release.yml publishes a bad JAR.
The maintainer's laptop is stolen. It has the only EA3 JDK, and EA3 is no longer available for download.
A power cut during release leaves partly uploaded artifacts.
Servers become ARM-only. EA builds are available only for x86.
Sanctions block downloads of OpenJDK EA builds in the maintainer's country.
The Clojure community boycotts libraries written by AI.
Each EA build lasts three months. Four builds come each year.
After ten years, Java 8 is not available in CI images.
The matrix test duration increases to four hours.
A shallow clone in CI gives version 0.1.1 and overwrites a published version.
The JVM makes all value objects == to each other.
Every field in every program is named __hash.
The JVM verifier rejects every class that has a constructor.
Java 8 gets value classes overnight through a back-port.
A tool translates all documentation into Latin and the English source is lost.
Each thread of a program sees a different value of the fallback property.
The class-file format becomes JSON.
A government bans preview JVM features in public-sector software.
The media blames value objects for a bank outage. Managers forbid value-type.
A heat wave throttles the maintainer's machine. Benchmark noise exceeds 30%.
A cosmic ray flips a bit in a cached capability result.
nREPL evaluates forms on a thread with no Compiler/LOADER binding.
A build tool caches macroexpansions on disk and replays them in a later JVM.
Operators call the capability report one million times per second.
Users cite a two-year-old benchmark as a performance guarantee.
Class.isValue disappears from every JVM on one day. Value classes still work.
